claims.claim: The deepest hole humans have ever dug
claims.source_checked: Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. Earth Environ. 7: 124, https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (full text, reference list); Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 -> arcticandnorth.ru: Russian PDF /upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf and English PDF /upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf (Arctic and North 44: 224-239), read in full incl. Figs. 2 and 5 rendered
claims.note: Zhu & Huang: SG-3 "remains the deepest vertical borehole ever attempted, reaching 12,262 m"; the deepest other vertical holes they list are X-1 (11,156 m) and SDTK-1 (10,910 m). Lobanov: "In 1990, the maximum depth was reached — 12262 m, which has not been surpassed so far." Lobanov's own label is narrower ("the world's deepest scientific well"), but Zhu & Huang carry the unqualified reading in true depth. "Dug" for drilled is framing.

claims.claim: ...was finished with a bit narrower than a dinner plate.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 -> arcticandnorth.ru: Russian PDF /upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf and English PDF /upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf (Arctic and North 44: 224-239), read in full incl. Figs. 2 and 5 rendered; USGS OFR 86-517, https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1986/0517/report.pdf (pdftotext); Met collection API v1/objects/201074 (accession 51.86.100)
claims.note: Lobanov: turbine "with a 214 mm drill bit"; Fig. 5c (actual well design) ends "d 215,9 мм / 12262 м", open hole below the 245 mm casing at 8770 m. USGS lists the turbo-coring bit ISM-214,3/60T. Met 51.86.100 "Dinner plate ... Diameter: 10 1/16 in. (25.6 cm)"; even the Met's smaller 'Dinner plate' 51.86.140 is 23.2 cm. "Finished with" correctly limits it to the last stretch (the mouth is 720 mm).

claims.claim: Drilling stopped in nineteen ninety-two, when its funding was cut.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 -> arcticandnorth.ru: Russian PDF /upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf and English PDF /upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf (Arctic and North 44: 224-239), read in full incl. claims.note: Lobanov: "However, a drastic reduction in funding made it impossible to continue the work. Drilling was stopped in 1992." Also: "In 1992, a unique operation was carried out to install a casing ... to continue drilling the well to a depth of 13 km. However, despite this, further drilling was abandoned." Zhu & Huang disagree on cause ("abandoned in 1992 when unexpectedly high bottom-hole temperatures of 212 °C induced plastic rock flow"); that sentence carries no citation and Lobanov nowhere mentions plastic flow (searched). The SOURCES block records the disagreement (A3).

claims.claim: Depth counter running alongside the year counter (keyframes 9,583 m at 1979, 12,000 m at 1983, 12,262 m at 1989, straight lines between)
claims.where: on-screen: Look 1 depth vs year animation (A6)
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 -> arcticandnorth.ru: Russian PDF /upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf and English PDF /upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf (Arctic and North 44: 224-239), read in full incl. Figs. 2 and 5 rendered
claims.note: Lobanov: "In June 1979, the well broke the record of 9583 meters held by the US well, reaching a depth of 9584 meters. In 1983, the well reached a depth of 12066 m"; "December 27, 1983, the well depth reached 12000 m"; after the 1984 string break "drilling was resumed from a depth of 7000 m" and "it took 6 years to reach 12 km depth again"; 12,262 m in 1990. The code (depthAt, index.tsx) keys 9,583 not 9,584 and interpolates 12,000 -> 12,262 linearly over 1983-89, so a paused frame shows e.g. ~12,066 m at '1985' and 12,1xx m in 1986-88, depths the record did not reach until the third branch in 1989-90. The year and depth counters also run on different clocks (20 vs 19 years plus a 5% hook offset). Change: key 9,584 m at mid-1979, 12,066 m by the end of 1983 and hold it flat to 1989, then 12,262 m at '1989–90', driving both counters from one clock; or hide the year counter while the depth runs. SOURCES item 9 should then describe the keys the code actually uses.

claims.claim: SOURCES item 2: "The USGS summary lists ... below 7 km, cavities wider than 40 cm"
claims.source_checked: USGS OFR 86-517, https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1986/0517/report.pdf (pdftotext); Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 -> arcticandnorth.ru: Russian PDF /upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf and English PDF /upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf (Arctic and North 44: 224-239), read in full incl. Figs. 2 and 5 rendered
claims.note: USGS says "The presence of cavities [caverns in the Russian] to depths of 7,000 m contributed to the complex configuration of the cross section" and, of the neutron-gamma log run to 11,440 m, "there is a sharp drop in intensity of secondary radiation where cavity diameter is greater than 40 cm". It does not place >40 cm cavities below 7 km. Lobanov does say caverns multiplied deeper than 7 km, but gives no size. Change to e.g.: 'USGS: cavities "to depths of 7,000 m", and log readings affected "where cavity diameter is greater than 40 cm"; Lobanov: below 7 km "the borehole took on an oval shape, many caverns appeared".' Script and labels unaffected.
